title: A collaborator shifts the blame in a meeting
description: The client eases off, seeing you as someone who will own it. Afterwards Chloe says, "Cheers — lunch on me next time." Your manager privately reminds you to "watch how you communicate next time".

choices.action: Fill your manager in on the facts so you do not become the permanent fall guy
Swallow it and do not pursue it

title: In-house kernel versus an open-source stack
description: Three weeks later security has traced the internal reports back to your team and invited you to a 'compliance conversation'. Beforehand your manager briefs you: 'Don't take all of it. Blame the misjudgement on the vendor or the upstream community so the team can close this.' In the room, the compliance lead already has the logs on the table.

choices.action: Use your manager's line and blame the upstream community
Admit you got the assessment wrong and accept whatever sanction is appropriate

title: Balancing a promising idea against delivery pressure
description: Three months of evenings produce a breakthrough and a solid case for the efficiency gain. When you ask your manager for formal resource, a colleague in the same sprint proposes a similar optimisation: it uses the current tech, ships sooner and gains less.

choices.action: Compare the two on depth and long-term return, and argue yours is worth the bigger investment
Back the quicker option, and get your work put on the roadmap for later

title: Pitching against a cheaper rival
description: You run the rival down in the pitch. One of the panellists turns out to know them, and the room cools: “We asked for your proposal, not a review of someone else’s.” You look small, and it costs you marks.

choices.action: Pull it back immediately and return to what your own proposal actually delivers
Keep going on about their past failures

title: Whether to tell your manager about a health problem
description: You hide it and push through, and for a while the work gets done. Then, on a critical piece of work, you run out of steam, and people start to speculate.

choices.action: Come clean now and adjust the plan
Keep hiding it and gamble that nobody notices

title: Lunch with the team, or keep the break to yourself
description: Your delivery stays solid, but in a review Warren says you “don’t really know the team’s pain points”. Missing lunch has left you out of the loop.

choices.action: Start joining lunch occasionally, specifically to catch up
Keep skipping the café, and book 1:1s with the people who matter

title: Your partner's job offer in another city: live apart, stay, or rethink
description: You find the nerve to talk to your manager about an internal move or remote working. The company does have a team in that city, but the role does not quite match your current direction. Going would mean proving yourself again and would slow promotion in the short term. What you and your partner both care about is being together.

choices.action: Take the move as a fresh start that broadens your CV
The terms of the move do not work, so stay and put up with the travel

title: Named on a department award you did not work on
description: Aurora wins. You are named at the awards. Three months later internal audit picks the pack for a spot check and asks you to describe exactly what you contributed to the platform.

choices.action: Admit you were not part of the core work
Invent a contribution that matches your manager’s story

title: A senior puts their name on an intern’s work
description: Rowan turns on you in the room. Your manager tells you to “sort it afterwards.” Quinn’s name is added. Rowan freezes you out.

choices.action: Walk your manager through the facts and ask for a fair rating
Take on some of Rowan’s work to thaw the relationship

title: After dinner, karaoke with someone on the promotion panel
description: You put in an appearance and leave. Helen texts: “Sensible to get some rest.” Someone on the team mutters that you do not mix.

choices.action: Bring breakfast in the next day for the people who stayed
Offer no explanation and let your work speak for itself

title: Late-night work messages and the manager's reaction
description: Chris says, "In principle that's fine, but we can't slip client deadlines."

choices.action: Set up an on-call rota, with no replies on days you are not on call
Keep to your hours anyway, whatever the reaction

title: Abnormal health-check results: push through or see a doctor
description: You deliver on time and the quarter looks excellent. At the end-of-month follow-up, the biopsy is another two weeks' wait. Meanwhile you get palpitations and fatigue, and your family starts pushing you to take it seriously. You can put it off again or stop the damage now.

choices.action: Get treatment now, and tell the team you need some time to adjust
Keep putting off the follow-up as one project follows another

title: An unpublished restructure, and a friend about to buy a flat
description: Sienna holds off signing. Two weeks later the change is announced and she thanks you. Your manager senses a leak and starts checking who knew.

choices.action: Go to your manager and admit you dropped a vague hint
Stay silent

title: A toxic team culture: stay or leave?
description: The VP hears about the letter. In an all-hands they say, without naming names, that anyone who cannot handle tough competition is free to leave. HR then sits you down. The CEO hired this VP personally, the company is fully behind the change, and are you willing to 'get with the programme'?

choices.action: Stand your ground, and ask HR to open a formal investigation into the culture
Go along with a transfer for now, and start looking for jobs elsewhere

title: The client praises a feature you did not build
description: The remaining payment comes in. Two months later the client finds there is no forecasting, and sends a solicitor’s letter alleging misrepresentation and asking for the money back.

choices.action: Produce the review recording and the scope pack in your defence
Go along with sales and accept “poor communication” as the explanation

title: A collaborator shifts the blame in a meeting
description: Your manager papers over it, but the client is not satisfied. Your manager asks why you did not explain in the room.

choices.action: Reply to the email at once with the facts, and take ownership of the fixes
Excuse it as "not the moment to speak"

title: Pushed on stage at the Christmas party
description: You get up and run a quick game for the whole room. It goes down better than you expected. People are laughing, and your manager gives you a thumbs-up. Afterwards the host tries to keep you up there for the next part.

choices.action: Quit while you are ahead: hand the stage back and return to your table
Ride the moment and keep hosting, even as you start to run out of steam

title: Raising a technical objection on another team's API design
description: Their owner thanks you for the private heads-up, admits it was an oversight, and is willing to change the design. They add, offhand: "Let's keep this between us — no need to air it in the channel, or it will look as if our review missed it." You need to decide whether to share the finding with the wider teams so others can learn from it.

choices.action: Agree the fix in the 1:1, then record the problem and the decision in the design doc
Anonymise it as a "performance review lesson" and share it with both teams

title: Emergency hotfix — do you skip the process?
description: The hotfix goes out in time and the live event carries on. When the process is completed afterwards, it finds an edge case the fix missed. The rollback is ready, so there is no second incident. The CTO asks you privately what would have happened if the rollback had failed.

choices.action: Admit the risk, and propose a pre-authorised emergency path that sets out when the process can be shortened
Stress that this success shows the team's skill with incidents, and argue for keeping the current flexibility
